outcome: Hospital co-admissions for mothers and babies
Birth interventions (induction, instrumental birth, caesarean section, epidural, episiotomy)
Special Care Nursery/Neonatal Intensive Care admission for infants
cohort: All women giving birth in New South Wales, Australia, between 2000 and 2012
finding: Women who accessed residential parenting services (RPS) in the year after birth were more likely to be socially advantaged, have higher rates of birth interventions, and experience more co-admissions and treatment for mental health disorders compared to women who did not access RPS.
mod_finding: This study did not examine mode of delivery as an outcome, but it did find that women admitted to residential parenting services had more labor and birth interventions than those not accessing these services.
